user.title: Set up Ban Guard
user.description:
Ban Guard manages Home Assistant's IP bans, adds an allowlist and protects against failed-login attacks. It makes no outbound network calls unless you turn on a feature that needs one.

Ban Guard never bans loopback, this host's own addresses, the Supervisor network or the address you are using right now.

data_description.protection_enabled: Ban addresses automatically after repeated failed logins. While on, Ban Guard replaces Home Assistant's `login_attempts_threshold`; it is restored when Ban Guard is removed or disabled.

abort.already_configured: Ban Guard is already set up.
abort.single_instance_allowed: Ban Guard is already set up.

protection.title: Failed-login protection
protection.description: Ban an address after too many failed logins within a time window. Each repeat offence uses the next step of the escalation ladder.

data_description.escalation: Comma-separated ban durations for the 1st, 2nd, 3rd… offence. Units: s, m, h, d, w. `permanent` may only be last. Example: `1h, 24h, permanent`.
data_description.network_overrides: One rule per line: `CIDR: threshold/minutes` or `CIDR: off`. Example: `192.168.0.0/16: 20/60`. The most specific network wins.
data_description.repeated_failures_threshold: Fire a `repeated_failures` event and notification at this count (0 turns it off).
data_description.attack_threshold: The "Under attack" sensor turns on when this many failed logins happen within the window, from any address.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.description: Ban Guard always fires the `ban_guard_event` event. Use the bundled blueprint to forward events to the mobile app.

data.notify_allowlisted_failures: Report failed logins from allowlisted addresses

logging.title: Activity log and allowlist
logging.description: The activity log is kept in `.storage/ban_guard.activity`. Query strings and credentials are never stored; secret parts of URLs such as webhook ids are redacted.

data_description.log_successful_logins: Record the address, browser and user of every sign-in through the login page. Reconnecting an already signed-in app or browser tab is not logged.
data_description.log_blocked_requests: At most one entry per address per minute.
data_description.allowlist_refresh_minutes: Hostname lookups use your system resolver, or DNS-over-HTTPS if enabled.

enrichment.title: GeoIP and DNS lookups
enrichment.description:
Each option below is off by default and makes outbound calls when turned on:

• **GeoIP** downloads the free DB-IP Lite database from `download.db-ip.com` once a month. Lookups happen locally; no addresses are sent. Data by DB-IP.com, licensed CC BY 4.0.
• **Reverse DNS** sends PTR queries for addresses shown in the panel to your system's DNS resolver.
• **DNS-over-HTTPS** sends those PTR queries, and allowlist hostname lookups, to the HTTPS endpoint below instead. The endpoint operator sees the addresses being looked up.

data.rdns_enabled: Enable reverse DNS (queries your DNS resolver)
data.doh_enabled: Use DNS-over-HTTPS (sends queries to the URL below)

data_description.geoip_edition: Country is about 8 MB. City adds city names and is about 130 MB; it is held in memory.
data_description.geoip_max_mb: Downloads larger than this are refused.

countries.title: Country rules
countries.description: Requires GeoIP. Use ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes separated by commas, for example `DE, AT, CH`. Private, loopback, allowlisted and protected addresses are never blocked by country. Addresses whose country is unknown are allowed.

npm.title: Nginx Proxy Manager sync
npm.description:
Push the ban list into one Nginx Proxy Manager access list that Ban Guard owns: its client rules are replaced on every sync with `deny` rules for each ban followed by `allow all`. Calls go only to the URL below. The password is stored encrypted.

Detected add-on: {addon}

data_description.npm_url: The admin interface, usually on port 81.
data_description.npm_password: Leave empty to keep the stored password.

npm_list.title: Choose the access list
npm_list.description: Pick an access list dedicated to Ban Guard. Its client rules will be overwritten.

error.invalid_threshold: The threshold must be at least 1.
error.invalid_window: The time window must be at least 1 minute.
error.invalid_duration: A duration is not valid. Use values like 30m, 1h, 7d or permanent.
error.invalid_escalation: The escalation ladder is not valid. Use values like `1h, 24h, permanent`; `permanent` may only be last.
error.invalid_override: A network override line is not valid. Use `CIDR: threshold/minutes` or `CIDR: off`.
error.invalid_country: Use two-letter ISO country codes such as DE or US.
error.country_conflict: A country cannot be both allowed and blocked.
error.invalid_doh_url: The DNS-over-HTTPS URL must start with https://.
error.cannot_connect: Could not connect to Nginx Proxy Manager.
error.invalid_auth: Nginx Proxy Manager rejected the credentials.
error.not_found: Nginx Proxy Manager API not found at this URL.
error.no_access_lists: Create an access list in Nginx Proxy Manager first.

failed_logins_24h.name: Failed logins in the last 24 hours

hook_incompatible.title: Ban Guard request protection is disabled
hook_incompatible.description: This Home Assistant version changed the internals Ban Guard hooks into ({detail}). Ban Guard turned off request blocking and automatic bans; Home Assistant's built-in banning keeps working. Ban list editing still updates `ip_bans.yaml`. Check for a Ban Guard update.

ip_ban_disabled.title: Home Assistant IP banning is turned off
ip_ban_disabled.description: Ban Guard needs `ip_ban_enabled: true` (the default) in the `http:` section of `configuration.yaml`. Until it is enabled, bans are recorded but not enforced.

hook_runtime_error.title: Ban Guard request protection stopped after errors
hook_runtime_error.description: Ban Guard hit repeated errors while checking requests ({detail}) and turned request blocking off to keep Home Assistant working. Home Assistant's built-in banning still works. Reload Ban Guard to try again, and please report the error.

geoip_failed.title: Ban Guard could not load the GeoIP database
geoip_failed.description: Downloading or reading the DB-IP Lite database failed: {detail}. Country information and country rules are unavailable until it succeeds.

npm_failed.title: Ban Guard could not sync to Nginx Proxy Manager
npm_failed.description: The last sync failed ({detail}). Check the URL and credentials in Ban Guard's options.

allow.name: Allowlist
